findings.description: From 1:50 to 5:50 this stall is clearly established: a red bin of oranges and yellow fruit, teal fruit in a light-blue crate in front of it, and a purple crate of peaches at the lower left. As the camera orbits in one continuous move, this arrangement never comes back into view. The same area turns into purple trays of purple fruit next to white boxes of green apples (6:25-6:75), then white boxes of tomatoes and purple trays holding peaches and teal fruit (7:75-8:25). The teal fruit is now in purple trays, not the blue crate, and the red bin is gone. By 9:00 it is rows of grey metal tables with purple-rimmed trays. A camera orbiting a nearly stationary subject should keep showing the same fixed stall from new angles, so the layout is morphing rather than being re-viewed.

The opening view sets up a narrow open-air street aisle: open sky and building facades, a long row of red patio umbrellas, and a dense crowd walking along it. During the continuous orbit (6:50-8:75) the background becomes an enclosed dim hall with a dark ceiling and fluorescent tubes. In the rear view (9:00-9:75) the space is a broad covered hall with long parallel rows of tables and only a few people. The crowded aisle and the red-umbrella row, which should still line up with the established street axis, are gone. The geometry of the space does not match the street layout established in the first five seconds.
